title: Bannister effect after the first 4-minute mile

tellings.quote: The Bannister effect is named after British athlete Roger Bannister, who broke the 4-minute mile record in 1954 at Oxford. Within just 2 and 1/2 years, 10 other runners had all broken the 4-minute mile.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes what he calls the Bannister effect, named after a British runner, Roger Bannister, who ran a mile in under four minutes at Oxford in 1954. Michels says that within about two and a half years, ten other runners had done the same. He uses it to make the point that once one person shows something is possible, others quickly follow.
